rationale:
Iteration 8 raced sensor_size 0.016 on top of the iteration 7 best. It scored 610.4, below the 688.5 best. The oval held at 20 of 20, but s-bend completion fell from 20 of 20 to 13 of 20, with 7 off-track endings and steering_oscillation at 0.38. The slalom stayed at 0 of 20 with max_error 0.0625 and 1.05 line-loss events. The Evaluator's own rule applies: the s-bend fell below 18 of 20, so sensor_size reverts to 0.012. The larger footprint smooths the s-bend signal and costs it completions without fixing the slalom.

The slalom is still blocked. Speed, sensor spread, kd, kp and sensor_size have each been tried, and max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.064. rms_error is low on every track, so the slalom losses are edge excursions on its alternating bends. With one action run left, I will not risk an untested slalom lever (sensor_size 0.008, ki, or sensor weights) on the scored race. I resubmit the iteration 7 best unchanged: kp 2.8, kd 0.9, ki 0, base_speed 1.1, the iteration 4 spread (x = -0.024 to 0.024 m), sensor_size 0.012, sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] and line_loss 'last_direction'. Expected result: about 688 on the development tracks, with oval 20 of 20, s-bend 20 of 20 and slalom 0 of 20.

Hypotheses for the next iteration: the slalom needs a lever other than speed, spread, kd, kp or sensor_size, such as ki, a sensor y offset, or the sensor_weights scale. The measurements requested are the slalom max_error and line_loss_events, which are the signals that would show whether a new lever helps.
